canada.title: After 18-year-old’s online exploitation and death, mom wonders why police didn’t search devices right away
canada.summary: An 18-year-old in St. John’s who died by suicide appeared to have been targeted for years by a global online child exploitation group yet police did not initially examine the teen’s phones and computers. Following an interview with CBC’s the fifth estate, the RCMP apologized to the family for not “properly” communicating “our offer/ability to further this investigation” and has since taken the devices for review.

lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the Pentagon’s recent complaints about Canada’s defence spending have not come up in his conversations with U.S, The Canadian Press reports.
Nova Scotia’s new Liberal leader calling on PC government to pause AI data centre, The Canadian Press reports.
Swiss officials said relations would be kept through North Korea’s embassy in Bern, and its own embassy in Beijing, BBC News reports.
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died, The Associated Press reports.
Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will also be a first: Organizers made an unprecedented decision to postpone the event to Saturday because of bad weather, The Associated Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
